node-1.label: A 17-year-old female had a 7-month history of intermittent lower extremity swelling, proteinuria, and hematuria.

node-2.label: A renal biopsy at another hospital 4 months prior suggested possible IgA nephropathy, and she was treated with the angiotensin receptor blocker valsartan but symptoms persisted; she had no history of drug use, infections, malignancy, or family history of hepatitis B or C, HIV, rheumatic disease, or tumors; she was normotensive, and both general physical and funduscopic examinations were normal; her lung fields were clear without rales or fremitus.

node-3.label: A 24-hour urine protein test showed a total protein level of 2.75 g; urinalysis revealed 24 erythrocytes per high-power field; serum levels of urea, creatinine, and albumin were within normal ranges; autoantibody tests were unremarkable, and serum antiphospholipase A2 receptor antibodies were negative; renal ultrasound findings were normal.

node-4.label: A review of the previous renal biopsy showed 22 glomeruli, with 1 (4.5%) showing global sclerosis and 1 (4.5%) showing focal segmental sclerosis; there was mild mesangial expansion, thickening of the glomerular basement membrane, endothelial swelling, focally swollen podocytes, and hypercellularity; swelling of the tubular epithelium and patchy infiltration of lymphocytes and monocytes in the interstitial area were noted, without interstitial fibrosis; the capillary walls in the interstitial area showed no lesions.

node-5.label: Immunohistochemical analysis revealed granular deposits along the capillary walls for IgM, C3, C1q, and kappa and lambda light chains, with mild staining for IgG and IgA; IgG subclass staining showed segmental positivity for IgG1 but negativity for IgG2, IgG3, IgG4, and antiphospholipase A2 receptor; granular deposits along the capillary walls, especially for lambda and C1q, indicated immune complexes; silver staining showed spike-like projections at the 3-o'clock position, indicating a spiked glomerular basement membrane around the immune complexes; Masson staining showed scattered fuchsinophilic deposits, indicating immune complexes; lesions of mesangial cells, endothelial cells, and podocytes were noted.

node-6.label: Lupus nephritis was excluded due to the absence of systemic lupus manifestations and negative immunoserological markers except for an antinuclear antibody titer of 1:100; no solid tumors or hematological malignancies were detected by computed tomography or hematological examinations, and all tumor biomarkers were negative.

Because THSD7A/NELL-1/EXT1/EXT2/PCDH7 testing is still unavailable, confidence is maintained at 0.45.

node-18.label: Secondary membranous nephropathy due to occult infection (e.g., hepatitis B, HIV, syphilis)

attrs.why: Current frontier is membranous nephropathy; the secondary subtype (node-14) remains possible (0.15) because infection workup is missing (nodes 12, 15). The IgG1-dominant, C1q/lambda-positive immune deposits (node-16) are more characteristic of secondary causes. This candidate refines secondary membranous nephropathy into a specific infectious etiology that is testable and could explain the atypical immunofluorescence pattern.

node-19.label: Secondary membranous nephropathy due to drug exposure (e.g., NSAIDs)

attrs.why: Current frontier is membranous nephropathy; NSAID/drug exposure history has not been obtained (node-15). Drug-induced membranous nephropathy is a known secondary cause and would fit the IgG1-dominant, C1q-positive deposits (node-16) that are atypical for primary anti-PLA2R-positive disease. This candidate refines secondary membranous nephropathy into a drug-induced subgroup that requires targeted history-taking.

node-20.label: Novel membranous nephropathy antigens beyond PLA2R and THSD7A — NELL-1, EXT1/EXT2, and PCDH7 — have not been tested.

node-21.label: Primary membranous nephropathy driven by a novel non-PLA2R antigen such as THSD7A or NELL-1

attrs.why: Membranous nephropathy is the leading diagnosis with anti-PLA2R negativity in both serum and tissue and IgG1-dominant, IgG4-negative capillary-wall deposits, a profile compatible with a non-PLA2R novel-antigen-driven primary membranous nephropathy; the laboratory physician specifically proposes a THSD7A or other novel-antigen-related primary subtype. Because THSD7A/NELL-1/EXT1/EXT2/PCDH7 have not been tested, this antigen-defined subtype remains plausible but unconfirmed, so confidence is 0.32.
